executiveSummary: Iteration 000044 implements the multi-PRD scaffolding across define, prototype, audit, and refactor phases with broad compliance. The Zod schema correctly adopts an array model for requirement_definition with preprocess-based backward migration. define-requirement, create-prototype, audit-prototype, and refactor-prototype all produce per-index artifacts with correct naming. Three gaps were found: (1) the scaffold template tmpl_state.json still initialises requirement_definition as a legacy single object instead of an empty array; (2) approve-prototype guardrail hard-codes legacy filenames (audit.json / refactor-report.md) rather than the new audit-report_NNN.json / refactor-plan_NNN.md names, causing it to reject a fully-completed multi-PRD flow; (3) the PR body inside approve-prototype hard-codes it_XXXXXX_refactor-report.md instead of reading actual refactor plan paths from state. Additionally, the approve-requirement output message changed from 'Requirement approved.' to 'All N requirement(s) approved.', breaking the backward-compat test US-003-AC08a.

verificationByFR.notes: define-requirement.ts correctly derives nextIndex = requirementDefinitions.length + 1 and zero-pads to 3 digits.
All produced artifacts (product-requirement-document_NNN.md, prototype-creation_NNN.json, audit-report_NNN.json, refactor-plan_NNN.md) follow the it_XXXXXX_<type>_NNN.<ext> pattern.

tmpl_state.ts defines RequirementDefinitionEntrySchema and wraps it in requirementDefinitionField = z.array(…). Same pattern applied to prototypeCreationField, prototypeAuditField, prototypeRefactorField.
z.preprocess in each field auto-migrates legacy { status, file } objects to [{ index: 1, status, file }].

approve-requirement only processes in_progress entries (not all non-approved entries as stated). A 'pending' entry remains unprocessed. Additionally, the changed success message ('All N requirement(s) approved.') breaks the backward-compat test US-003-AC08a which expects 'Requirement approved.'.
create-prototype sets state.phases.prototype.prototype_creation to an array; audit-prototype sets prototype_audit; refactor-prototype sets prototype_refactor.
auto.ts calls runCreatePrototype, runAuditPrototype, runRefactorPrototype — each command internally iterates over all PRD entries in index order.

scaffold/.agents/tmpl_state.json still initialises requirement_definition as { "status": "pending", "file": null } (legacy object), not [] as required. It also initialises prototype_creation, prototype_audit, prototype_refactor as single objects.

approve-prototype correctly reads all PRD entries and consolidates Goals into CHANGELOG. However: (a) the guardrail checks legacy filenames it_XXXXXX_audit.json and it_XXXXXX_refactor-report.md rather than the new per-PRD names (audit-report_NNN.json / refactor-plan_NNN.md), causing the command to abort with 'audit not found' when only new-format files exist; (b) the PR body hardcodes it_XXXXXX_refactor-report.md instead of reading refactor plan paths from state.phases.prototype.prototype_refactor.

verificationByUS.notes: All five ACs satisfied: _001/_002/…md naming, no overwrite, state array updated, approved-guard works, typecheck passes.
AC01 not fully met: only in_progress entries are approved, not every entry in the array. AC03 confirmation prompt exists but changed output message breaks US-003-AC08a backward-compat test.
create-prototype reads all approved requirement_definition entries, iterates user stories per PRD, and stores prototype_creation as an array.
audit-prototype produces it_XXXXXX_audit-report_NNN.json per PRD index and stores prototype_audit as an array.
refactor-prototype iterates over prototype_audit entries, produces it_XXXXXX_refactor-plan_NNN.md per entry, and stores prototype_refactor as an array.

Zod schema auto-migrates legacy state at parse time (AC01, AC02). However, the scaffold template (the initial state new projects receive) still uses the legacy format, meaning new projects start with a non-array state that must be migrated on first read. The backward-compat test US-003-AC08a fails due to changed output message.
auto.ts delegates to the three phase commands (create/audit/refactor prototype), each of which handles multi-PRD iteration internally.

AC01, AC02 (CHANGELOG merge with per-PRD prefixes) and AC04 (gh unavailable skip) are satisfied. AC03 partially: PR body includes all PRD Context/Goals but the refactor report path is hardcoded to the legacy it_XXXXXX_refactor-report.md, not the new it_XXXXXX_refactor-plan_NNN.md files tracked in state. AC05 (typecheck) passes.

minorObservations: approve-requirement generates a single it_XXXXXX_PRD.json even for multiple PRDs (last-wins in the loop). The file is used only as a legacy fallback in create-prototype, so this is low-risk, but could be surprising.

The progress.json entries reference audit_artifact_path and refactor_report_path pointing to legacy names (it_000044_audit.json / refactor-report.md). These fields appear unused by core commands but may confuse tooling.
The confirmation prompt in approve-requirement (AC03) is a UX improvement but blocks non-interactive CI runs that previously passed without --force.
approve-prototype guardrail logic also fails to read state.phases.prototype.prototype_audit / prototype_refactor, meaning it has no awareness of state-tracked completion.
conclusionsAndRecommendations: The multi-PRD feature is substantially implemented and functional for the primary workflow. Three areas require fixes before the iteration can be marked complete: (1) Update scaffold/templates to initialise requirement_definition, prototype_creation, prototype_audit, and prototype_refactor as empty arrays []; (2) Fix approve-prototype guardrail to also check for new per-PRD audit-report_NNN.json / refactor-plan_NNN.md files (via state or glob), not only legacy filenames; (3) Fix approve-prototype PR body to read refactor plan paths from state.phases.prototype.prototype_refactor instead of hardcoding the legacy path. Additionally, update the US-003-AC08a test to expect the new success message 'All 1 requirement(s) approved.' to restore the passing test suite.
